english.title: Possess article with blade / sharply pointed article on school / further education premises
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without good reason or lawful authority, had with you on

(A)_[school]_
(B)_[further education]_

premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..),

(C)_[an article which had a blade or was sharply pointed, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..)]_
(D)_[a folding pocket knife which had a blade the cutting edge of which exceeded 7.62 centimetres or three inches]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139A(1) and (5) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
have with you on school premises / further education premises an article with a blade / sharply pointed OR
a folding pocket knife with blade cutting edge exceeding 7.62cm (3 inches)

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) ‘school premises’ is defined in section 139A(6) as land used for the purposes of a school excluding any land occupied solely as a dwelling by a person employed at the school.
(ii) 'further education premises' is defined in section 139A(6A) as land used solely for the purposes of an institution within the further education section or a 16-19 academy.
(iii) A defence is available at section 139A(4) if a person can prove he had the weapon for the use at work, educational purposes, religious reason or as part of any national costume. A defence of good reason or lawful authority is also available via 139A(3).
(iv) Section 139A was amended to extend the offence to cover not only school premises but also further education premises; for offences committed before 6th April 2022 please see H8777.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 139A(5)(a) and (5ZA) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
Sections 139A(5A) -(5E) outline provisions requiring a court to impose an appropriate custodial sentence in certain cases.
